name: Round 1: The Bidding MCQ
description: 4 Options • Point Bidding • Universal Tech Fundamentals

questions.q: When you type 'google.com' in a browser, where does the operating system look first to find the IP address?
questions.expl: The operating system checks its local cache first to save network lookup time.

questions.q: Why does data disappear from RAM when the computer powers off, but stays safe on an SSD?
options: SSDs use non-volatile Flash NAND cells
questions.ansText: SSDs use non-volatile Flash NAND cells
questions.expl: RAM requires constant electrical charge (volatile); SSDs trap electrons permanently in NAND cells.

questions.q: When clicking a link and you get '404 Not Found', what does the first digit '4' signify?
questions.expl: 4xx status codes mean the client requested a resource or URL that does not exist.

questions.q: 4 employees earn ₹25,000, but the CEO earns ₹1,00,00,000. Which metric best represents typical employee salary without distortion?
questions.expl: Outliers distort the arithmetic mean; the median gives the true central tendency.

questions.q: Where does 'Cloud Computing' physically exist in the real world?
options: In massive air-conditioned data centers across the globe
questions.ansText: In massive air-conditioned data centers across the globe
questions.expl: Cloud computing is renting computing resources hosted in global enterprise server farms.

questions.q: During flash sales or railway booking, why do payments succeed but tickets fail to book?
questions.expl: Thousands of users attempt to reserve the final seat simultaneously, triggering transactional locks.

questions.q: How does Google Autocomplete predict your search query in milliseconds as you type?
options: Trie (Prefix Tree) Data Structure & Search Frequency
questions.ansText: Trie (Prefix Tree) Data Structure & Search Frequency
questions.expl: Trie trees store billions of common search phrases in memory for fast instant prefix matching.

questions.q: What core protection does 'HTTPS' provide over traditional 'HTTP'?
options: End-to-End SSL/TLS Encryption of transit data
questions.ansText: End-to-End SSL/TLS Encryption of transit data
questions.expl: HTTPS encrypts network packets so eavesdroppers on public Wi-Fi see only scrambled ciphertext.

questions.q: What is the primary difference between traditional programming and Machine Learning?
options: Traditional code uses hand-coded rules; ML learns rules from data patterns
questions.ansText: Traditional code uses hand-coded rules; ML learns rules from data patterns
questions.expl: Humans write rules in software; ML algorithms discover patterns and create predictive models from historical data.

questions.q: Why did JSON largely replace XML as the standard data interchange format on the web?
options: Lightweight, human-readable, and natively parsed by JavaScript
questions.ansText: Lightweight, human-readable, and natively parsed by JavaScript
questions.expl: JSON eliminates heavy tag overhead and maps directly to native JavaScript key-value objects.

questions.q: What does browser 'Incognito / Private Mode' actually do?
options: Hides you completely from government & hackers
Prevents local saving of history and cookies on your device
questions.ansText: Prevents local saving of history and cookies on your device
questions.expl: It only stops local session storage; your ISP, network admin, and destination websites still log your IP.

questions.q: Which database type is best suited for social networks, friend recommendations, and connection graphs?
questions.expl: Graph databases treat nodes and relationships as first-class citizens, making link traversal instant.

questions.q: What operating system concept allows you to play music, code, and browse websites simultaneously on one CPU?
questions.expl: The CPU scheduler switches execution contexts in microsecond time slices, giving the illusion of concurrency.

questions.q: If an internet connection is advertised at 100 Mbps, why is maximum download speed ~12.5 MB/s?
questions.expl: ISPs measure in bits (small b), while computer files are stored in bytes (capital B).

questions.q: In Git version control, what is a 'Commit' conceptually equivalent to in video games?
questions.expl: A commit saves a permanent snapshot of code state that can be rolled back anytime.

questions.q: What cyber attack involves trying millions of password combinations automatically every second?
questions.expl: Brute force attempts every possible key permutation until the password unlocks.

questions.q: What web technology allows websites to behave like installable native mobile apps with offline support?
questions.expl: PWAs use Service Workers and web manifests to deliver app-like experiences without app store installation.

questions.q: When an AI hiring model favored male applicants over female applicants, what caused this error?
options: Training Data Bias (historical company hiring data favored men)
questions.ansText: Training Data Bias (historical company hiring data favored men)
questions.expl: 'Garbage in, garbage out' — machine learning reproduces human biases present in historical training records.

questions.q: Classical computers store information as 0 or 1. What quantum property allows storing both 0 and 1 simultaneously?
questions.expl: Superposition enables qubits to evaluate exponentially more combinatorial paths at once.

questions.q: Why does calling an API 10,000 times in one minute return HTTP Status '429 Too Many Requests'?
questions.expl: Rate limiting protects servers from resource starvation, cascading failures, and DDoS attacks.

questions.q: If 1 Byte equals 8 Bits, how many bits make up one 'Nibble'?
questions.expl: A nibble is a four-bit aggregation, equal to half of an octet (byte).

questions.q: If power fails during a bank money transfer between withdrawal and deposit, what ensures money isn't lost?
questions.expl: Atomicity guarantees 'all or nothing' execution; any incomplete step reverts all changes to the clean initial state.

questions.q: When a computer powers on, what low-level firmware program boots the OS into RAM?
questions.expl: Basic Input/Output System performs hardware power-on self tests (POST) and hands control to the OS loader.

questions.q: In business analytics, what does 'Customer Churn Rate 20%' mean?
options: 20% of customers cancelled or stopped using the service
questions.ansText: 20% of customers cancelled or stopped using the service
questions.expl: Churn rate is the percentage of subscribers or customers who discontinue subscriptions over a period.

questions.q: What malware encrypts computer storage drives and demands payment to restore access?
questions.expl: Ransomware locks critical system data using cryptographic ciphers until a ransom is paid.

questions.q: What front-end performance technique delays image loading until the user scrolls them into viewport?
questions.expl: Lazy loading reduces initial page bundle size and conserves client data by deferring offscreen assets.

questions.q: What recommendation system algorithm powers YouTube and Amazon 'Customers also bought' feeds?
questions.expl: Collaborative filtering builds predictions about user interests by collecting preferences from many similar users.

questions.q: Why is thermal paste applied between the CPU die and the metallic heatsink?
options: To eliminate microscopic air gaps and maximize heat transfer
questions.ansText: To eliminate microscopic air gaps and maximize heat transfer
questions.expl: Air is a poor heat conductor; thermal paste ensures seamless conductive thermal dissipation to cooling fans.

questions.q: What is the industry term for showing two variations of a button to different user segments to measure conversion?
questions.expl: A/B testing evaluates two variants against user metrics to determine which variant statistically performs better.

questions.q: While AWS S3 handles static images, what storage type is required for low-latency database engines?
options: Block Storage (e.g., AWS EBS / NVMe Volume)
questions.ansText: Block Storage (e.g., AWS EBS / NVMe Volume)
questions.expl: Databases require raw block-level read/write operations with sub-millisecond I/O latency.

name: Round 5: Future or Fired? (4-Team Debate)
description: 4-Team Battle • 60-Second Timed Speeches • Industry Reality Verdict

questions.topic: AI coding assistants (Claude, Copilot) will eliminate 70% of entry-level developer roles within 5 years.
questions.expl: AI automates boilerplate code, but complex system design, security, and domain problem-solving require human engineers.

questions.topic: In the future, nobody will need to write code because No-Code drag-and-drop tools will build all enterprise apps.
questions.expl: No-Code handles simple marketing websites; custom enterprise logic, scalability, and algorithmic security always demand code.

questions.topic: With high-speed 5G and fiber cloud, local PC hard drives will disappear in favor of 100% Cloud PCs.
questions.expl: Services like Windows 365 and Shadow PC prove dumb terminals with cloud virtualization are cost-effective and secure.

questions.topic: Browsing in 'Incognito / Private Mode' guarantees absolute anonymity from internet service providers and network monitors.
questions.expl: Incognito only discards local device history; upstream ISPs, corporate routers, and government authorities still log traffic.

questions.topic: Because of its beginner-friendly syntax, Python will completely replace languages like Java, C++, and JavaScript.
questions.expl: Browsers strictly execute JavaScript; high-performance game engines require C++/Rust. Python's interpreted runtime is too slow.

questions.topic: Within 10 years, traditional desktop towers and laptops will vanish, with smartphones docking directly as our sole computer.
questions.expl: Flagship mobile silicon already rivals desktop CPUs; docking systems like Samsung DeX showcase single-device computing.

questions.topic: Since social media apps like Instagram and YouTube are free to use, they collect nothing of financial value from users.
questions.expl: 'If you are not paying for the product, you are the product.' Personal telemetry data fuels multi-billion-dollar ad auctions.

questions.topic: By 2035, physical government paper currencies will be abolished, replaced entirely by decentralized Bitcoin.
questions.expl: Central banks are launching Central Bank Digital Currencies (CBDC e-Rupee) rather than yielding sovereign monetary control.

questions.topic: Because ChatGPT can automatically generate data charts, the profession of Data Analyst is dead.
questions.expl: AI outputs numbers; human analysts connect data patterns to executive business strategy and identify hidden context.

questions.topic: Future international conflicts will be determined not by artillery, but by cyber warfare crippling electricity and banking grids.
questions.expl: Modern state-sponsored warfare consistently deploys cyber attacks targeting electrical grids and financial infrastructure first.

questions.topic: When practical Quantum Computers arrive, all current RSA banking encryption will be cracked in seconds.
questions.expl: Shor's algorithm will compromise current public-key crypto, which is why NIST is standardizing Post-Quantum Cryptography now.

questions.topic: By 2030, all Indian roads will feature 100% driverless autonomous commercial vehicles.
questions.expl: Unpredictable road conditions, stray animals, and density necessitate at least two more decades before full autonomous adoption.

questions.topic: Physical corporate IT offices will disappear entirely, with 100% of technology employees working from home forever.
questions.expl: Full remote isolation degrades mentorship and creative synergy; enterprise companies overwhelmingly adopt hybrid models.

questions.topic: A university degree is no longer necessary to land top software engineering careers; GitHub portfolios and skill suffice.
questions.expl: Silicon Valley giants and startups have dropped strict degree mandates in favor of verified open-source and coding competence.

questions.topic: Brain-computer interfaces like Neuralink will allow humans to type and interact with computers using thought alone.
questions.expl: Paralyzed human trial participants have already successfully controlled computer cursors and played chess using neural implants.

questions.topic: Generative AI art tools (Midjourney) will completely extinguish the careers of digital artists and UI/UX designers.
questions.expl: AI produces raw imagery; human designers define user psychology, brand coherence, responsive ergonomics, and empathy.

questions.topic: Traditional passwords will be entirely obsolete within 5 years, replaced by biometric Passkeys.
questions.expl: The FIDO alliance (Google, Apple, Microsoft) is actively phasing out master passwords in favor of cryptographic device passkeys.

questions.topic: Open-source AI models (Meta Llama, Mistral) will surpass and commoditize closed proprietary models like OpenAI.
questions.expl: Global open-source community fine-tuning runs circles around centralized proprietary models for specific edge use-cases.

questions.topic: Augmented reality Smart Glasses will replace smartphones in our pockets within the next decade.
questions.expl: Products like Meta Ray-Ban and Apple Vision demonstrate wearable spatial audio and heads-up computing are the next frontier.

questions.topic: Electric cars are completely green, with zero total environmental impact throughout their manufacturing lifecycle.
questions.expl: Lithium/Cobalt mining and fossil-fueled grid charging generate carbon emissions; renewable energy transition is mandatory.

questions.topic: Within 20 years, AI surgical robots will execute complex human operations with higher precision than human doctors.
questions.expl: Computer vision already outperforms human radiologists in tumor detection, moving towards semi-autonomous microsurgery.

questions.topic: Governments will legally ban smartphones and social media platforms for children under the age of 16.
questions.expl: Countries like Australia have already drafted landmark legislation barring young adolescents from predatory social algorithms.

questions.topic: People will stop clicking 10 blue search links on Google, turning exclusively to direct conversational AI answers.
questions.expl: Perplexity and ChatGPT Search showcase that users prefer concise verified synthesis over wading through ad-bloated links.

questions.topic: Satellite internet like Starlink will render undersea subsea fiber optic cables obsolete.
questions.expl: Satellites lack aggregate bandwidth; 99% of global internet traffic travels across ultra-high-capacity undersea fiber cables.

questions.topic: Sending all raw sensor data to distant cloud centers is inefficient; AI chips must run locally on edge devices.
questions.expl: Autonomous vehicles cannot afford network latency to apply emergency brakes; inference must execute locally on the edge.

questions.topic: AI models will soon be trained predominantly on AI-generated Synthetic Data rather than scraped human text.
questions.expl: With high-quality human internet text exhausted, curated synthetic reasoning data is becoming essential for frontier model training.

questions.topic: Microservices are over-engineered for 90% of startups; a well-built Monolithic server is cheaper and faster.
questions.expl: Distributed systems introduce immense networking overhead and debugging complexity; modular monoliths offer superior early velocity.

questions.topic: Individual engineers won't be able to innovate in AI; only 2-3 global mega-corporations will control artificial intelligence.
questions.expl: While frontier cluster training requires billions of dollars, open-source model optimization keeps independent innovation alive.

questions.topic: Cash will be totally eliminated in India by 2030, with Central Bank Digital Rupee handling 100% of transactions.
questions.expl: Despite stellar UPI adoption, informal rural economies and power failure contingencies ensure physical currency endures.

questions.topic: AI software developers will soon produce 100% bug-free software that never crashes.
questions.expl: Software requirements change constantly; edge cases, runtime anomalies, and shifting user expectations ensure bugs always exist.

name: Round 6: The Tech Millionaire
description: KBC Style High-Stakes Questions • 4 Options • 50:50 Lifeline

questions.q: Why does Netflix stream ultra HD video in India instantly without buffering, even though master servers reside in the USA?
options: Content Delivery Network (CDN) edge caches installed inside local ISP networks
questions.expl: Netflix pre-caches popular movie files onto Open Connect storage appliances directly inside local ISPs.

questions.q: Why do mobile banking OTP security codes automatically expire after 5 or 10 minutes?
questions.expl: Enforcing short TTL prevents malicious interceptors from reusing captured tokens later.

questions.q: Which memory tier inside a computer operates with the fastest access latency?
questions.expl: CPU SRAM cache operates directly on the processor die with sub-nanosecond clock cycle latency.

questions.q: In historical Titanic passenger data analysis, which demographic cohort showed the highest survival percentage?
questions.expl: Privileged top-deck cabin proximity and the maritime protocol of 'women and children first' maximized their survival rate.

questions.q: How does Google search crawl billions of web documents and return relevant results in under 0.2 seconds?
questions.expl: Like an index at the back of a textbook, Google maps search keywords to pre-compiled document IDs in advance.

questions.q: Why does a factory-sealed 1,000 GB external hard drive report only ~931 GB in Windows Explorer?
options: Manufacturers count in Decimal (1000^3) while OS counts in Binary (1024^3)
questions.expl: Manufacturers define 1 GB = 1,000,000,000 bytes; operating systems calculate 1 GiB = 1,073,741,824 bytes.

questions.q: Why did Microsoft submerge a sealed data center container 117 feet deep onto the ocean floor in Scotland?
options: Free natural seawater cooling & oxygen-free nitrogen environment avoiding corrosion
questions.ansText: Free natural seawater cooling & oxygen-free reliability (Project Natick)
questions.expl: Underwater data centers eliminate costly mechanical air conditioning and reduce server hardware failure rates.

questions.q: What is the technical term when an AI chatbot invents non-existent historical facts with high confidence?
questions.expl: LLMs predict the next most statistically probable token without an inherent grounded factual truth database.

questions.q: Why is 'correct horse battery staple' mathematically more secure against brute force than 'P@$$w0rd'?
options: Password Length (Entropy) scales combinatorics far higher than short symbol complexity
questions.expl: An 8-character complex password takes minutes to crack; a 28-character passphrase takes millennia to brute force.

questions.q: If you accidentally delete a critical tracked file in a Git repository, what command restores it from HEAD?
questions.expl: git restore discards unstaged working tree changes and retrieves the clean copy from the repository index.

questions.q: What international benchmark unit measures the operational computation speed of supercomputers?
questions.expl: Exascale supercomputers like Frontier are measured by how many quintillion floating-point calculations they solve per second.

questions.q: On New Year's Eve when food orders spike 50x in one hour, what cloud architecture prevents server crash?
questions.expl: Auto-scaling dynamically provisions additional stateless virtual instances and routes incoming request spikes evenly.

questions.q: What cyber attack floods a web server with coordinated traffic from thousands of infected zombie botnets?
questions.expl: DDoS exhausts network bandwidth and server connection queues so legitimate users cannot access the service.

questions.q: Why do shoes you viewed on an e-commerce site follow you as advertisements onto Instagram and news sites?
options: Cross-site Tracking Cookies & Ad-Network Device Fingerprinting
questions.expl: Ad networks embed tracking pixels across publishers to build unified behavioral profiling IDs.

questions.q: Where did the computer engineering term 'Bug' literally originate from in 1947?
options: A real moth trapped inside a relay switch of the Harvard Mark II computer
questions.ansText: A real moth trapped in the Harvard Mark II computer
questions.expl: Computer pioneer Grace Hopper taped an actual moth into her logbook annotated: 'First actual case of bug being found.'

questions.q: What was the title of the very first video ever uploaded to YouTube in April 2005?
questions.expl: Co-founder Jawed Karim uploaded an 19-second video standing in front of elephants at the San Diego Zoo.

questions.q: How do commercial passenger airplanes at 35,000 feet altitude maintain high-speed internet connectivity?
options: Satellite Tracking Antennas & Ground-to-Orbit Microwave Beams
questions.ansText: Satellite Tracking Antennas & Ground-to-Orbit Microwave Beams
questions.expl: Airplanes feature roof-mounted radome antennas dynamically tracking geostationary and LEO satellites.

questions.q: What enabled computer scientist Katie Bouman and the EHT team to capture the first image of a Black Hole in 2019?
options: 5 Petabytes of radio telescope data stitched via specialized Python algorithms
questions.ansText: 5 Petabytes of radio data stitched via Python algorithms
questions.expl: Algorithms synthesized synchronization data collected across 8 global radio observatories acting as one Earth-sized telescope.

questions.q: Why were keyboard keys arranged in the scrambled 'QWERTY' layout rather than alphabetical order?
options: To intentionally slow down typists so mechanical typewriter metal arms wouldn't jam
questions.ansText: To prevent mechanical typewriter key arms from jamming
questions.expl: Christopher Sholes separated frequently co-occurring English letters to prevent mechanical linkage collisions.

questions.q: How does Google Maps calculate live street traffic delays and color road segments in red or green?
options: Crowdsourced GPS telemetry and speed velocity streaming from active Android phones
questions.ansText: Crowdsourced GPS telemetry streaming from active smartphones
questions.expl: When clusters of phones on a road segment slow down, algorithms detect congestion and flag the route in red.

questions.q: What is the official expanded engineering acronym of 'Wi-Fi'?
options: Wi-Fi is NOT an acronym; it was a catchy branding rhyme
questions.ansText: Wi-Fi is NOT an acronym; it was a catchy branding rhyme
questions.expl: The Wi-Fi Alliance hired a branding firm to coin a consumer-friendly name for the dry technical standard IEEE 802.11b.

questions.q: Does enabling 'Dark Mode' on an OLED or AMOLED display genuinely reduce battery consumption?
options: Yes, up to 30% battery savings because black OLED pixels physically turn completely off
questions.ansText: Yes, black OLED pixels physically shut off completely
questions.expl: Unlike backlit LCDs, each individual OLED diode emits its own light; displaying true black draws zero current.

questions.q: Which 10th-century monarch's initials form the two runic symbols inside the Bluetooth wireless logo?
options: King Harald Bluetooth (Nordic Runes Hagall and Bjarkan)
questions.ansText: King Harald Bluetooth (Nordic Runes Hagall and Bjarkan)
questions.expl: The Scandinavian telecom alliance honored King Harald who united Scandinavia just as Bluetooth unites gadgets.

questions.q: Which female NASA computer scientist wrote the asynchronous priority software saving the Apollo 11 moon landing?
questions.expl: Her priority scheduling architecture dropped non-critical radar radar tasks, allowing the lunar module computer to focus on descent thrusters.

questions.q: What was the very first commercial '.com' domain name ever registered in internet history in 1985?
questions.expl: A Massachusetts computer manufacturer registered Symbolics.com, pioneering the commercial dot-com era.

questions.q: What is the true secondary purpose behind Google asking users to click street signs and crosswalks in CAPTCHAs?
options: Human labeling and training datasets for Waymo autonomous self-driving AI models
questions.ansText: Human labeling datasets to train autonomous vehicle vision AI
questions.expl: reCAPTCHA uses millions of human clicks daily to train computer vision models identifying road hazards.

questions.q: What physical material was used to craft the world's very first computer mouse invented by Douglas Engelbart in 1964?
options: Carved Wood with two metal wheels
questions.ansText: Carved Wood with two metal wheels
questions.expl: The prototype was carved out of a wooden block with two perpendicular wheels tracking horizontal and vertical coordinates.

questions.q: Where on Earth are giant dessert statues of Android versions (KitKat, Oreo, Donut) permanently displayed?
options: Googleplex HQ Lawn in Mountain View, California
questions.ansText: Googleplex HQ Lawn in Mountain View, California
questions.expl: Google's headquarters campus features a public garden of oversized statues celebrating every Android code name.

questions.q: What fundamental engineering design flaw triggered global fears of the Y2K (Year 2000) computer millennium bug?
options: Legacy software stored dates using only 2 digits ('99' becoming '00' interpreted as 1900)
questions.ansText: Legacy software stored dates using only 2 digits ('99')
questions.expl: To conserve expensive memory in the 1970s, programmers stored years as two digits, causing calendar rollover glitches.

questions.q: Who is universally celebrated in history as the world's very first computer programmer in 1843?
questions.expl: Ada Lovelace wrote the first published algorithm intended to be executed by Charles Babbage's mechanical Analytical Engine.

name: Round 7: Rapid Fire Clash
description: Fast 30-Second Clock • Direct Options • Maximum Velocity Challenge

questions.q: What is universally recognized as the central 'Brain' of a computer system?
questions.expl: The CPU fetches, decodes, and executes software instructions.

questions.q: Which foundational language provides the semantic structural skeleton of all web pages?
questions.expl: HTML defines the elements, links, and content hierarchy of the web.

questions.q: What is the smallest indivisible unit of digital data in computer science?
questions.expl: A bit represents a single binary state: voltage high (1) or voltage low (0).

questions.q: Which Git command saves current staged changes permanently to local repository history?
questions.expl: git commit writes a permanent checkpoint snapshot with an explanatory message.

questions.q: Which declarative language is the worldwide standard for querying relational database records?
questions.expl: SQL allows developers to filter, join, and aggregate structured tables.

questions.q: Which platform commands over 90% of global internet search engine market share?
questions.expl: Google handles over 8.5 billion search queries per day.

questions.q: What is the standard universal keyboard shortcut to 'Copy' selected text on Windows?
questions.expl: Ctrl + C copies the active selection to system clipboard memory.

questions.q: Which parent corporation engineers and maintains the open-source Android mobile operating system?
questions.expl: Google develops Android and licenses the Google Mobile Services suite.

questions.q: What unique numerical label identifies every computer connected to the internet network?
questions.expl: IP addresses route packets across networks to their precise destination.

questions.q: What software tunnel secures your personal internet traffic when connected to untrusted public Wi-Fi?
questions.expl: A VPN encrypts all data packets between your machine and the VPN exit server.

questions.q: Which web technology defines presentation style, colors, fonts, and responsive layout of websites?
questions.expl: CSS styles raw HTML into visually stunning, responsive user interfaces.

questions.q: What is the standard universal keyboard shortcut to 'Paste' clipboard data on Windows?
questions.expl: Ctrl + V inserts the contents of the clipboard into the active document.

questions.q: In binary computer computation, exactly how many Bytes make up 1 Kilobyte (KB)?
questions.expl: Binary systems scale by powers of 2; 2^10 equals 1024.

questions.q: Who is universally recognized as one of the primary 'Fathers of the Internet' for designing TCP/IP?
questions.expl: Vint Cerf and Bob Kahn designed the underlying TCP/IP protocol suite.

questions.q: Which Git command uploads committed local repository changes to a remote server like GitHub?
questions.expl: git push transmits commits to the specified upstream remote branch.

questions.q: In SQL databases, which command permanently erases an entire table along with its structural schema?
questions.expl: DROP TABLE deletes both the schema definition and all row data permanently.

questions.q: How many total addressable bits comprise a standard IPv4 internet address?
questions.expl: IPv4 uses 32-bit addresses formatted as 4 dot-decimal octets (e.g. 192.168.1.1).

questions.q: In Python programming, is a standard List object Mutable (modifiable) or Immutable?
questions.expl: Python lists can append, pop, and alter element values in-place without reallocation.

questions.q: What is the official name of the open-source Linux kernel penguin mascot?
questions.expl: Tux stands for (T)orvalds (U)ni(X).

questions.q: What standard Windows keyboard shortcut reverses and cancels your most recent text edit action (Undo)?
questions.expl: Ctrl + Z pops the recent action off the software undo history stack.
